-- IGProtocol scaffold: VINIT → IMSCRIB → AFWD → CLINK → AFWD → FSPLIT → EVALT → AFWD → FSPLIT → EVALT → EVALF → ENGAGR → FFUSE → AREV → IFIX → TANCH
-- (native ob3ect designer; elaborate against the kernel to verify)
name: test entity
notes:
Auto-designed from: Design an Ob3ect for:

test entity

phase_0.boundary_condition: test runner lifecycle from instantiation to sealed result
phase_0.justification: Auto-designed by the native Ob3ect Auto-Designer (in-process candle, no Python)

AFWD.justification: forward morphism that evaluates a single assertion and produces an outcome

AREV.justification: reverse morphism that releases fixtures and rolls back state after verdict determination

CLINK.justification: sequential composition of multiple assertions into a single test execution path

ENGAGR.justification: assertion that simultaneously passes and fails across retries, held as live contradiction

EVALF.justification: constructive refutation that an assertion does not hold under current state

EVALT.justification: constructive affirmation that an assertion holds under current state

FFUSE.justification: arms rejoin into a single Belnap verdict: T if all pass, F if any fail, B if both pass and fail present

FSPLIT.justification: single execution forks into passing, failing, and contradictory arms based on assertion outcomes

IFIX.justification: append-only permanent record of verdict and assertion outcomes written to test history

IMSCRIB.justification: self-reference preserving test case identity across setup, execution, and teardown phases

TANCH.justification: final immutable record containing verdict and all assertion outcomes, closed to further mutation

VINIT.justification: test case object allocated but no assertions executed, no verdict assigned

phase_2.fuse_result: single Belnap verdict (T, F, or B) encapsulating all assertion outcomes
phase_2.rejoin_note: each arm processes its assertions (EVALT/EVALF/ENGAGR), then FFUSE joins them into one verdict; fork always closes
phase_2.split_input: test case after all assertions executed
phase_2.verdict_reason: FSPLIT3 at step 6 dangles — no matching FFUSE3

phase_3.both_description: at least one assertion affirmed and at least one refuted (or flaky), verdict register 11
phase_3.false_description: at least one assertion refuted, no contradictory assertions, verdict register 10
phase_3.void_description: test case instantiated, no assertions run, verdict register 00

steps.domain_action: test case instantiated in uninitialized state
first assertion affirmed, pass arm active
second assertion executed on pass arm
second assertion affirmed, pass arm continues
second assertion refuted, fail arm activated
flaky assertion detected, both arms held simultaneously
pass, fail, and contradictory arms reconciled into single verdict
teardown fixture executed, state rolled back
verdict and all assertion outcomes appended to permanent test log

phase_5.alfs_store: test specification repository serves as canonical reference for test definitions
phase_5.compiler_frontend: test framework translates test definitions into executable assertion sequences
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: test runner communicates with assertion engine via result callbacks and verdict channels
phase_5.memory_mechanism: fixture state held in transient memory; verdict log persisted to append-only store
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: test executor determines assertion order, retry policy, and parallelization

phase_6.cycle_cost: one test execution cycle consumes fixture setup/teardown resources and assertion evaluation compute
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — fixture state returns to baseline, only irreversible log growth remains
phase_6.post_cycle_state: fixtures released, log extended by one sealed verdict entry
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: test case uninitialized, fixtures pristine, log at prior length
